model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book, residual income equivalent (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: FY2026 distributions not yet paid at the valuation date
equity_bridge.note: 60% payout of FY2026E EUR6,150m = EUR3,690m (EUR500m H2-2026 buyback approved July 2026 + dividend/2027 buyback), plus the unexecuted tail of the EUR1.0bn FY2025 programme (~EUR0.2bn), less the part of the H2 programme likely executed by late October (~EUR0.15bn), discounted ~0.6yr at 11%. Projected flows start FY2027 off a TBV already net of these distributions, so this is not double-counted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (shareholders' equity FY2020 EUR54,774m -> FY2025 EUR69,015m)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR diverges >30% from equity CAGR: the 5yr EPS CAGR is meaningless off FY2020 EPS of EUR0.06 (restructuring trough) and the 3yr 8.1% includes the FY2024 litigation dip. Tangible book per share (FY2020 EUR23.18 -> FY2025 EUR32.06, +6.7%/yr) outgrew equity because of ~EUR4.3bn of buybacks over 2021-25.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs FY2022 27,063 -> FY2025 31,434 (3yr) and FY2020 24,011 -> FY2025 (5yr). Free cash flow is not meaningful for a bank (operating cash flow swung from -28.6bn in FY2024 to +47.1bn in FY2025 on deposit and trading balance movements), so no FCF CAGR is reported; the owner flow is distributable earnings.

scenario_narratives.base: Deutsche Bank keeps compounding from its restructured base: RoTE climbs from ~10% in FY2026 to 12.5% by FY2028 and holds, slightly short of the >13% target, with cost/income in the low 60s/high 50s and credit costs near 35-40bp. Growth in tangible book slows from 4% to 2.5% as RWA growth normalises, and the bank distributes 67-80% of profit via dividends and buybacks. On a 11% cost of equity this is worth ~1.2x tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Global Hausbank plan over-delivers: Q2 2026's 14% RoTE becomes the through-cycle level by FY2029, CIR falls below 60%, and German infrastructure/defence spending plus asset gathering in DWS and the Private Bank lift growth to 5% a year near-term. The market re-rates the stock from below book to ~1.4x tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bear: The credibility discount proves right: investment-banking revenue mean-reverts, ECB cuts squeeze NII, CRE and private-credit exposures lift provisions, and a large litigation outcome lands. RoTE falls back to ~8% -- below the 11% cost of equity -- so growth destroys value and the bank is worth less than its tangible book.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth its tangible book plus the present value of the returns it earns above its cost of equity on that book. Distributable earnings (profit after AT1 coupons less the capital retained to grow risk-weighted assets) are discounted at an 11% cost of equity with no net-debt deduction, because deposits and wholesale funding are the bank's raw material, not claims ahead of equity. The share price sits at 0.87x tangible book, which only makes sense if RoTE settles below the cost of equity -- the bear case -- whereas the bank is currently earning 11-14%.
key_risks_to_valuation: RoTE durability: each 1pt of sustained RoTE moves value by roughly EUR3.7/share (TBV EUR60.5bn / (CoE - g) / 1,909m shares)
Cost of equity: 11% is judged; a market demanding 12-13% for European G-SIBs explains most of the gap to the share price
Litigation and enforcement outcomes (cum-ex, 1MDB trial late 2026, Polish FX mortgages, US AFC investigations)
Investment Bank revenue cyclicality -- FIC/IBCM fee pools were unusually strong through H1 2026
Basel III final/output-floor and FRTB RWA inflation reducing distributable capital
Share price fell ~21% from EUR35.6 (Aug 2026) to EUR27.9 into the Q3 print without a company-specific disclosure in the extracted filings; Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-28 may move the FY0 anchor

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 23.815-35.845
data_sources.financials: Deutsche Bank Annual Report FY2025 and Interim Report as of June 30, 2026 (consolidated balance sheet, Non-GAAP tangible book and basic shares tables, income statement attributable profit lines); Metrics.csv FY2015-H1 FY2026
data_sources.qualitative: DBK.DE_Analysis.json (2026-10-25): 2028 targets RoTE >13%, CIR <60%, CET1 13.5-14.0%, 60% payout; Q2 2026 RoTE 14.0%, CIR 58%

inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment is expensed inside compensation and benefits (equity statement line FY2025: EUR30m; deferred equity awards are hedged with treasury-share purchases). The flow stream is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders, already after that expense, so no separate SBC deduction is made and the share count is held flat on the basic-shares-outstanding basis, which already includes 30.1m vested share awards.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:37:14Z regular XETRA close (Friday); Q3 2026 results due 2026-10-28 -- refresh price and anchors then
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,909.2m basic shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (1,910.6 issued - 31.5 treasury + 30.1 vested awards), H1 2026 interim, Non-GAAP 'Basic shares outstanding' table. Held flat: buybacks executed after 30 Jun are paid out of the FY2026 distribution added back in the equity bridge, so reducing the share count as well would double-count them.
inputs.tangible_book_anchor: Tangible shareholders' equity EUR61,505m at 30 Jun 2026 (TBVPS EUR32.22; book EUR68,616m less EUR7,111m goodwill/intangibles ex DWS minority share). Projected FY2026 year-end TBV after deducting FY2026 distributions: ~EUR60.5bn -- the base off which RoTE and retention are computed. Price/TBV = 0.87x.
inputs.fy0_anchor: FY2026E profit attributable to DB ordinary shareholders (after AT1 coupons) EUR6,150m = H1 2026 actual EUR3,433m + H2 estimate ~EUR2,720m (H2 2025 was EUR2,434m = FY2025 5,797 - H1 3,363; +12% for the Q2 run-rate +14% YoY and the ~EUR33bn revenue guide). FY2025 actual EUR5,797m (Annual FY2025 line 7803).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single cost of equity of 11.0% across scenarios, in EUR: 10y Bund ~2.7% + levered beta ~1.4 x 5.5% ERP = 10.4%, plus ~0.5pt for a G-SIB with open litigation (cum-ex criminal probe, Polish FX mortgages, US$1.1bn 1MDB suit to trial late 2026) and a 2016-2019 history of capital raises. Scenario risk is carried in the RoTE paths, not in the discount rate (charged once). The 'wacc' field in each scenario is this cost of equity.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease costs sit inside noninterest expenses and therefore inside net income; no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flow is profit attributable to Deutsche Bank ordinary shareholders, i.e. after NCI (mainly DWS minority, H1 2026 EUR110m) and after AT1 coupons (H1 2026 EUR417m). AT1 (EUR12.1bn) and NCI (EUR1.6bn) are excluded from tangible book.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank route per dcf-methods SKILL.md (Bank -> residual income on tangible book), implemented as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, as for NAB.AX. Engine mapping: 'revenue' = profit attributable to ordinary shareholders; 'ebitda_margin_path' = distributable FCFE as % of that profit = 1 - (TBV growth x opening TBV)/profit, i.e. the capital that must be retained to grow RWA at the assumed rate while holding CET1 in the 13.5-14.0% range; D&A, capex, tax, SBC and WC are zero because profit is already after all of them. Net debt = 0: deposits, long-term debt (EUR111bn) and repo funding are operating funding for a bank, not financing claims ahead of equity. Under constant RoTE and growth this is algebraically the residual-income value TBV x (RoTE - g)/(CoE - g). Driver paths were derived from explicit RoTE and TBV-growth paths (see each scenario's rationale). FY0 is FY2026E (H1 actual + H2 estimate) so year 1 = FY2027; FY2026 distributions not yet paid at the valuation date are added in the equity bridge.

bear.rationale: RoTE 9.0% FY2027 and 8.0% thereafter: an IB/FIC revenue reversal from unusually strong 2025-H1 2026 fee pools, ECB cuts compressing NII, CRE/NBFI provisions and a fresh litigation charge (cum-ex, 1MDB, Polish FX mortgages), with Basel output-floor RWA inflation forcing retention. TBV growth 2.5% then 2%. Implied NI FY2028 EUR5.0bn, below FY2025's EUR5.8bn. Terminal multiple = 1.02/0.09.

base.rationale: RoTE 11.75% FY2027, 12.5% FY2028 and flat thereafter -- management's >13% 2028 target is treated as a stretch that is narrowly missed (Q2 2026 printed 14.0% but H1 was 11.1% after Q1 bank levies; FY2025 10.3%). TBV growth 4%/4%/3.5%/3.5%/3% then 2.5% terminal, consistent with RWA growth (RWA +8% YoY to EUR367bn at Jun-26) slowing toward nominal GDP. Implied NI FY2027 EUR7.25bn, FY2028 EUR8.0bn. Payout capacity 67% rising to 80% -- above the 60% policy floor, consistent with the stated distribution of excess capital above 14% CET1. Terminal multiple = (1+g)/(CoE-g) = 1.025/0.085.

bull.rationale: RoTE 12.5% FY2027, 13.5% FY2028 (target beaten), 14.0% sustained -- the Q2 2026 run-rate made durable by CIR falling below 60%, German fiscal expansion and continued fee growth in DWS/Private Bank. TBV growth 5%/5%/4.5%/4%/3.5% then 3% terminal. Implied NI FY2028 EUR8.8bn. Terminal multiple = 1.03/0.08.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12.06x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 growth default: a G-SIB with a decade of missed targets before 2022, heavy IB cyclicality and several open litigation matters warrants a fatter bear tail, while the bull is supported by targets already being met (FY2025 RoTE >10%, CIR <65%) and Q2 2026 printing 14% RoTE.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
